newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - May 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - May 2.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Australian Bureau of Statistics figures released yesterday show full-time ordinary wages grew by 4.6 per cent after seasonal adjustment in the 12 months to February, possibly ruling out the prospect of the Reserve Bank of Australia making a further interet rate cut. Page 1.

Century Zinc Ltd will go ahead with its A$1.2 billion mine after obtaining support from the 12 necessary native title claimants. The company will now apply to the Queensland Government to resurrect the joint A$90 million Aboriginal compensation deal orignally offered, and issue licences for the mine to proceed. Page 3.

Federal Attorney-General Daryl Williams last night defended the High Court and warned politicians they should not recklessly attack the judiciary. Williams' defence follows attacks by both State and Federal politicians over the Wik case, which Williams said undermined public confidence in the judiciary. Page 4.

Following a series of polls indicating Independent MP Pauline Hanson's political party One Nation was gaining significant support, Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer and Trade Minister Tim Fischer took a tougher stance than that of Prime Minister John Howard, criticising Hanson's immigration, Aboriginal and foreign investment policies. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Despite the Liberal backbench refusing to reject Prime Minister John Howard's 10-point plan to resolve the Wik uncertainty after a five-hour meeting yesterday, the Nationals will meet their leader Tim Fischer next week and demand he tell Howard to pull ou of his plan in favour of full extinguishment over native title. Page 1.

Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer said yesterday Independent MP Pauline Hanson's One Nation Party's vision would destroy Australia's relationship with Asia and cost thousands of jobs if implemented. Downer's attack, mainly on Hanson's stand againt foreign investment and immigration, is the first from a Federal minister. Page 1.

Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge is under intense pressure to re-extend his Government's offer of A$30 million compensation to ensure the A$1.2 billion Century Zinc mine proceeds, following an agreement yesterday with all 12 Aboriginal claimants for their upport for the mine. Page 1.

A taskforce commissioned by the Federal Government to advise on shipping reforms recommended yesterday A$150 million should be cut from shipping costs by allowing Australian ships to employ cheap overseas labour and forcing the ships to compete with forein vessels to carry domestic cargo. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Despite being prepared to push Prime Minister John Howard into a position of outright extinguishment of native title, the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Affairs backbench committee have agreed to allow Howard to provide more detail on his 10-point lan before making a final decision on it, a move recognised by Howard as a significant development. Page 1.

New South Wales Police Commissioner Peter Ryan said yesterday State Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research figures showing an increase in crime across the State - the biggest increase in ten years - reflected the turmoil experienced in the State Police Srvice as a result of low morale caused by the Wood Royal Commission's removal of key officers. Page 1.

Former New South Wales MP and former Lord Mayor of Wollongong Frank Arkell was yesterday arrested at his Wollongong home and charged with 29 child sex offences by officers of the Child Protection Enforcement Agency. The offences date back as far as 1973.Page 1.

A confidential review says thousands of frail elderly people in New South Wales have been unable to gain access to home care support over the past five years, while young disabled people have received an increased number of hours of care. The situation paces many elderly people at risk of being admitted to nursing homes. Page 3.
THE AGE

A baby girl was born in Melbourne three weeks ago, and Melbourne scientists are hailing her birth as another world first in vitro fertilisation technology, after she was conceived using a method allowing a fertilised embryo to grow in a laboratory for fiv days before being transferred to a woman's uterus. The method could double the success rate for childless couples. Page 1.

Following the damning report by the Victorian Auditor General last week on the State's ambulance service contracts, several companies that lost out in the bidding process to Intergraph are considering legal action against the Victorian Government, with on company claiming it spent A$750,000 on the bids for the Metropolitan Ambulance Service dispatch system and other emergency service bids. Page 1.

Many Melbourne residents are frowning about the lights used to depict a place of glamour for the Crown Casino , with Inter-Church Gambling Taskforce spokesman Reverend Tim Costello saying the marketing of the complex has a hidden agenda. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard yesterday endorsed his Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer after Downer attacked Independent MP Pauline Hanson's agenda, saying it would destroy jobs, damage Australia's reputation overseas, and that it ought to be dropped However, Howard steered away from condemning Hanson outright. Page 1.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
